title: Automating Legacy Migration for Financial Systems
business: A mid-sized regional bank managing a monolithic core banking system written in legacy Java.
problem: The engineering team is overwhelmed by repetitive refactoring tasks required to modernize legacy modules, preventing them from focusing on high-level architectural design and new feature development.
solution: By deploying Devin as an autonomous collaborator, the bank offloads the repetitive engineering work of refactoring legacy codebases, allowing human engineers to shift their focus toward system architecture and strategic problem solving.
steps: Grant Devin read/write access to the legacy repository and existing CI/CD pipelines.
Define architectural constraints and coding standards within the project documentation for Devin to follow.
Task Devin with isolating specific legacy modules and rewriting them into modular microservices.
Review Devin's generated pull requests for scope discipline and adherence to codebase standards.
Merge validated code into the production branch after automated verification.
outcome: The engineering team transitions from manual code maintenance to acting as architects, resulting in faster modernization cycles and reduced technical debt.
limitation: Devin may struggle with highly proprietary, undocumented business logic that requires deep institutional context; verify this by checking if the agent produces code that a human maintainer would actually merge.
